customs: People may ask direct questions. Short, clear answers are normal.
Keep your passport, visa papers, address, and school or work information easy to reach.
At the airport, ask staff for help if you are lost. Use simple sentences.
At a service counter, wait for your turn and leave space for the person who is speaking with staff.
Ask someone to repeat an unfamiliar place name, and check the spelling before following directions or booking a ride.
Keep your destination written clearly, including the apartment number. Showing it can help when street names sound similar.
Before leaving an information desk, repeat the terminal, exit, or meeting point to check that you understood correctly.

customs: Many official websites end in .gov. Be careful with look-alike websites.
Keep digital and paper copies of key documents in safe places.
For immigration questions, use official information, your school office, or a qualified lawyer.
Use the same name and spelling shown on your identification. Ask staff how to enter a name on a form.
If a question on a form is unclear, ask for an explanation before you write or choose an answer.
Check the date format and say the month aloud when confirming a deadline. Ask which office handles your question.
Keep any confirmation message or reference number after submitting a form. It can help you ask about its progress.

customs: Read the lease before you sign. Ask questions in writing.
Take photos when you move in. Keep proof of damage you did not make.
Quiet hours, guest rules, parking, pets, and trash rules are common.
Ask which costs are included in the rent and which you pay separately. Request the details before making plans.
Roommates may share kitchen and bathroom space. Talk about cleaning, visitors, and shared supplies before problems become frustrating.
Check how to contact the landlord or manager for routine repairs, and ask which number handles urgent building problems.
Before moving out, ask about the building's checkout process, key return, and inspection. Keep the written instructions for reference.

customs: Report repair problems early. Use photos when possible.
Some apartments require you to sort trash, recycling, and large items.
Utility bills usually arrive every month. Late payment can add fees.
When reporting a repair, include your apartment number, the room, and when the problem began so staff understand the request.
A repair visit may have an arrival window rather than an exact time. Ask how you will receive updates.
Ask where to report a broken shared appliance or building light. Different problems may go to different service teams.
Confirm whether a repair request is complete before ending the call. Save the reference number and any appointment message.

customs: Keep receipts for returns, rent, deposits, and large payments.
Never pay a stranger with gift cards, crypto, or wire transfer for an emergency call.
Ask about monthly fees, ATM fees, minimum balances, and overdraft fees.
At a bank counter, give other customers space while they discuss their accounts. Wait until a staff member calls you.
Ask staff to explain an unfamiliar charge in simple words. A written fee list can help you compare the details.
Before leaving, check the amount on your receipt and ask about anything you do not recognize or understand.
If an unexpected caller claims to be your bank, contact the bank using a number you already know is genuine.

customs: The price tag may not include sales tax. The final price can be higher.
Return rules are different at each store. Keep the receipt and package.
It is normal to ask staff, "Excuse me, where is...?"
If you cannot find an item, describe what it is used for or show staff a picture of the product.
At checkout, wait until the previous customer has finished paying. Some stores use one line for several registers.
If a shelf price and register price differ, politely ask staff to check the label before you finish paying.
For a return, start by saying what you bought, when you bought it, and whether you want an exchange or refund.

Taking leftovers home is normal. Ask for a box.
Tell restaurant staff about allergies clearly before you order.
Some restaurants ask you to wait near the entrance for a table. Others have customers order at a counter.
Ask whether you order and pay at the table or counter if you are unsure how the restaurant works.
You can ask for separate checks before ordering when eating with a group. Ask whether the restaurant can arrange this.
When ordering takeout, confirm the pickup name and number of items. Check that you have the complete order before leaving.

customs: Driving rules and license rules are different by state.
Seat belts are expected. Car insurance is required in many situations.
For buses, check the route, direction, and last service time.
Let people leave a bus or train before you board, and keep bags out of the aisle and empty seats.
Check how to pay before your trip. Different services may use tickets, transit cards, an app, or other payment methods.
Ask whether a transfer needs another ticket or payment. Do not assume that nearby services use the same fare system.
Use the stop name as well as a nearby landmark when asking for directions. Repeat unfamiliar names to confirm them.

customs: Call 911 for a serious emergency. Say your address first.
For non-emergency sickness, a clinic or urgent care may be faster than the ER.
Ask for an interpreter if medical English is hard. It is important to be exact.
At reception, give your name and appointment time. Ask where to wait and whether there are forms to complete.
Bring a written list of your questions so you can explain what you want to discuss during the visit.
If you do not understand a question or instruction, ask the staff member to explain it again in simpler words.
Before leaving, ask whom to contact with questions about the visit and how you will receive any follow-up information.

Ask for language help if school papers are difficult.
When contacting the school, give your child's full name and class so staff can direct the message to the right person.

Check the school's visitor and pickup instructions before arriving. Ask the office how to report a change in pickup plans.
Keep permission slips and school messages in one place. If a deadline is unclear, ask which date the form is due.

Ask how to report a problem with equipment or supplies. Explain what happened and where help is needed.
Check who can approve a schedule change before making arrangements. Keep a copy of the updated schedule or confirmation message.

customs: Many offices leave voicemail. Check it often and call back.
Do not share passwords or verification codes with callers or strangers.
Text messages are common for quick plans, but formal issues may use email.
When leaving voicemail, say your name, reason for calling, and callback number slowly. Repeat the number at the end.
If a call drops, call back and explain that the connection ended. You can ask the person to repeat anything missed.
Before choosing a plan, ask which charges are included and whether there are extra costs for the services you need.
If you need a written record of a service change, ask for an email or text confirming the details.

customs: Write the apartment or unit number clearly. Missing numbers can cause lost mail.
USPS mail forwarding helps with postal mail, but it does not update every company or agency.
Tell banks, schools, doctors, employers, and important offices your new address directly.
Write the sender's and recipient's addresses clearly, and ask staff where each address should go if you are unsure.
At the counter, explain when the item needs to arrive. Ask staff to compare the available mailing options and prices.
Keep the mailing receipt and any tracking number. Use them when asking the carrier about the status of a package.
Ask your building manager where deliveries are left and how residents are notified. Buildings may use different package collection systems.

customs: Call 911 for fire, serious danger, or urgent medical problems.
For non-urgent problems, use a local non-emergency number or building manager.
Keep basic supplies: water, medicine, flashlight, chargers, and copies of documents.
When calling for emergency help, answer the call-taker's questions about your location and what happened as clearly as you can.
Be ready to give the phone number you are calling from. Stay on the line until the call-taker tells you to hang up.
If you call 911 by mistake, explain what happened to the call-taker rather than simply ending the call without speaking.
Learn the names of nearby streets and building entrances. These details can help you explain where assistance is needed.

customs: People often use small talk about weather, weekends, pets, or local places.
A smile and "How are you?" can be a greeting, not a long question.
Libraries and community centers can help with English, forms, computers, and local information.
For a first conversation, introduce yourself and keep questions simple. Give the other person room to end the conversation politely.
Ask before borrowing something or using another person's belongings. Agree on when and how you will return a borrowed item.
If someone invites you to an event, confirm the time and place. Ask whether you should bring anything with you.
When discussing a shared-space problem, describe the issue calmly and make a specific request instead of blaming a neighbor.

Clean the lint trap before or after using a dryer if the machine has one.
Some apartments have shared laundry rooms with posted hours and rules.
Check the posted payment instructions before loading a machine. A laundry room may use coins, a card, or an app.
Set a timer so you know when your cycle ends. Take your clothes out promptly when other people are waiting.
Keep folding tables and walkways clear of bags and baskets. Leave shared surfaces ready for the next person to use.
If a machine stops or takes your payment without starting, note its number and ask staff how to report the problem.

At pickup, compare the items with your ticket and check the requested work. Ask staff about any concern before leaving.

customs: For app rides, check the car, license plate, and driver's name before getting in.
At airports, rideshare pickup may be in a special area, not directly outside baggage claim.
Use the app or meter price. Be careful if a stranger offers a private ride inside the airport.
Confirm the destination before the trip starts, especially when several nearby buildings or streets have similar names in the app.
Ask where to wait if the pickup area is crowded. Describe a visible sign or entrance to help the driver find you.
If you need help with luggage, ask politely and explain which bags belong to you. Keep the pickup area clear.
Before leaving the car, check the seat and floor for your belongings. Keep the trip receipt for later questions.

Some gas pumps ask for a ZIP code when you pay by card.
If the car has a serious problem, move to a safe place before calling for help.
When paying inside a gas station, tell the cashier your pump number and the amount or fuel type you want.
Ask whether a parking space has a time limit before leaving your car. Check nearby signs as well as the meter.
When arranging a repair, describe the problem and when it happens. Ask for an estimate before agreeing to the work.
Keep your parking or repair receipt until you have checked the details. Ask whom to contact if a charge is unclear.

If the stylist suggests a change, ask them to explain it before agreeing. It is fine to request your original plan.
If you cannot keep an appointment, contact the salon as early as possible and ask about its cancellation or rescheduling policy.

dialogue.text: Would you like a tour?

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Yes, please. Do you have a month-to-month plan?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Yes. There is no long contract.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Great. Can I try one class first?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Yes. You can book a trial class at the front desk.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Is the class included in the trial price?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: This class is included. Here is the list of other charges.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Thank you. How do I cancel if I decide to join later?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: The cancellation steps are here. Please read them before signing up.

vocabulary.definition: a place or person who helps with problems
a place for missing items
a number used to track a problem
a person who can make decisions
a report about a problem
contact again later about the same issue
words that explain what something looks like or is like
information such as a phone number or email address
a record showing that you bought an item
something provided in place of a lost or damaged item
find an answer or solution to a problem
give a found item to staff or another responsible person

customs: Stay calm and specific. Say what happened, when it happened, and what you need now.
Ask for a receipt, email, ticket number, or case number after reporting a problem.
If the first person cannot help, politely ask who can make the decision.
Describe a lost item with details such as its color, size, and a distinctive feature. Avoid giving only a general name.
For a billing or order problem, have the receipt or order number ready. Explain the difference between what you expected and received.
Ask when and how you should follow up, and write down the contact details so you reach the correct team.
Before ending the conversation, repeat the agreed next step. A clear summary helps both you and the staff member avoid misunderstandings.

dialogue.text: Excuse me, I left my backpack on the bus.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: What bus route and what time?

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Route 12 at about 4:30 p.m.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Please fill out this lost item form.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Thank you. Can I get a case number?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Yes. It is 318. What does the backpack look like?

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: It is dark green with a small yellow patch on the front.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Please add that description and your contact number to the form.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: When should I check back if I have not heard anything?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Call this office tomorrow afternoon and give us your case number.
